title: Community Land Act, 2016
content: Community land is held by communities and managed through registered community assemblies and committees. Transactions require community consent procedures. Verify registration status and minutes of consent with the community register and county office.

title: Environment and Land Court — general guidance
citation: Environment and Land Court Act, No. 19 of 2011
content: Land ownership, boundaries, tenancies tied to land, and environmental disputes are heard by the Environment and Land Court. Filing requires title documents, search results, survey reports, and correspondence. Consider mediation where the court offers it.

title: Land Act, 2012
content: The Land Act governs land administration, management and tenure, including leases, licences, compulsory acquisition, and the rights of landlords and tenants in relation to land. Verify tenure type, approvals, and compensation procedure with the registry or Environment and Land Court guidance.

title: Adverse possession claims
content: Long, open, exclusive occupation may ground adverse possession claims with strict proof over many years. Get advice before asserting or conceding. Keep occupation evidence and payment records.

title: Verifying agents and sellers of land
content: Confirm agency registration, written authority from the owner, and registry records before paying deposits. View the land with documents in hand. Keep authority letters and messages.

title: Buying apartments on sectional titles
content: Flats carry sectional unit titles plus shared common property managed by owners corporations. Review service charge and management records. Keep the sectional title and management accounts.

title: Using Ardhisasa for land services
content: Ardhisasa handles searches, transfers, charges, and cadastral maps with eCitizen login and digital payments. Verify parcel numbers before transacting. Keep payment receipts and application references.

title: Beacons and survey disputes
content: Only licensed surveyors should fix or confirm beacons with mutation forms. Moving beacons is an offence. Keep survey reports and mutation records.

title: Boundary suits in the ELC
content: Boundary cases file with titles, searches, survey reports, and demand history in the ELC. Courts may order site visits. Keep pleadings and survey maps together.

title: Land boundaries and disputes — general guidance
content: Verify title deeds, mutation forms, and beacons through an official search and licensed surveyor before fencing or building. Boundary disputes may be resolved through the land registrar, the Environment and Land Court, or alternative dispute resolution. Keep search slips and survey reports.

title: Lodging cautions and restrictions
content: Claimants can lodge cautions warning against dealings pending disputes, with restrictions for stronger protection. Wrongful cautions attract costs. Keep the caution receipt and case filings.

title: Change of user and development permission
citation: Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019
content: Converting agricultural to commercial or multi-dwelling use needs planning approval with public notice. Build only after approval. Keep approval letters and plans.

title: Using title as loan security
content: Charges over land need spousal consent where applicable, valuation, and registration with statutory sale procedures on default. Read the charge before signing. Keep the charge and loan records.

title: Charges and mortgages over land — general guidance
content: A charge is a registered security that lets a lender recover a loan from the land if the borrower defaults, with notice and statutory sale procedures applying. Borrowers should understand interest, default, and redemption rights before signing charge documents. Keep copies of the charge, loan agreement, and all payment receipts.

title: Chief-led boundary settlements
content: Minor boundary disagreements can be settled by chiefs with survey input and written witnessed agreements. Serious or violent cases go to the registrar or ELC. Keep the settlement record.

title: Land owned by companies
content: Company land dealings need board authority and signatory proof with active company status. Check for charges at the registry and BRS. Keep resolutions and search results.

title: Completion statement on land purchase
content: Completion balances price against deposit, duty, fees, and apportionments with a signed statement. Pay through traceable channels. Keep bank slips and the completion statement.

title: Compensation for compulsory acquisition
content: Affected owners claim land value, developments, disturbance, and relocation costs through inquiry with valuations. Object to low awards promptly. Keep titles, valuations, and acquisition notices.

title: Compulsory acquisition and compensation — general guidance
content: The State may compulsorily acquire land for a public purpose but must pay prompt and full compensation to affected owners and occupants following due process. Affected persons are entitled to notice, inquiry, and an opportunity to claim compensation for land, developments, and losses. Keep title documents, valuation records, and all acquisition notices.

title: Consent to transfer charges
content: Some leases and scheme lands need landlord or board consent before transfer. Apply early with the sale agreement. Keep the consent letter with completion documents.

title: Land Control Board consent — general guidance
content: Dealings in agricultural land generally require Land Control Board consent within a strict time limit, failing which the transaction may be void. Attend the board with IDs, title, sale agreement, and consent fees. Keep the consent letter and meeting records.

title: Controlled transactions and Land Control Board consent — general guidance
content: Sales, transfers, leases, charges and subdivisions of agricultural land in a land control area generally need Land Control Board consent within the statutory period. Parties usually apply to the local board for the area where the land lies and attend the hearing together. Keep the application, board letter of consent, and transfer documents.

title: Customary tenure and adjudication
citation: Land Adjudication Act; Community Land Act, 2016
content: Unregistered customary holdings are adjudicated and registered progressively. Follow the local adjudication notices and objections. Keep hearing notices and determination records.

title: Demolition orders and enforcement notices
citation: Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019
content: Unapproved structures attract enforcement and demolition notices with appeal windows. Respond in writing and regularise where possible. Keep notices, plans, and appeal filings.

title: Deposits on land deals
content: Deposits should be recorded with refund terms, timelines, and default consequences, ideally held by advocates. Avoid cash to strangers. Keep deposit agreements and receipts.

title: Discharging a charge after repaying
content: After full repayment, obtain a discharge signed by the lender and register it to clear the title. Confirm the registry record is clean. Keep the discharge and new search.

title: Eviction from land needs a court order
content: Occupants can only be removed through lawful notice and court process, never by demolitions or force. Seek urgent orders where threatened. Keep title proof and demand letters.

title: Spotting fake title deeds
citation: Land Registration Act; DCI fraud guidance
content: Compare paper, seals, parcel numbers, and registry records; fake titles often mismatch TIMS-style green-card history. Insist on registry searches. Keep suspect documents for DCI.

title: Fencing and access road disputes
content: Fences should follow confirmed boundaries and approved access; blocking shared roads invites court orders. Resolve with survey and chief or ELC process. Keep survey reports and demand letters.

title: Forest and public utility land warnings
content: Excisions of forest or utility corridors sold cheaply are usually fraud. Verify gazette status and registry records. Keep search results and survey confirmation.

title: Freehold tenure in Kenya
content: Freehold gives absolute ownership subject to lawful planning and rates. Verify the title type on the deed and registry before buying. Keep the title and search certificate.

title: Gifts of land between family
content: Family gifts need transfer forms, consent where applicable, and registration like sales. Oral gifts are unenforceable. Keep the transfer, consent, and new title.

title: The green card (parcel file)
content: The green card at the registry records every transaction on a parcel. Inspect it during disputes to trace ownership history. Keep copies of entries relied upon.

title: Group ranches and subdivision
citation: Land (Group Representatives) Act; Community Land Act
content: Group ranch subdivisions follow member registers and consent procedures with titles issued per share. Verify membership and minutes. Keep register extracts and titles.

title: Family disputes over ancestral land
citation: Law of Succession Act; ELC guidance
content: Ancestral land sales without heir consent are challenged through succession objections, cautions, and ELC suits. Gather family meeting minutes and heir lists. Keep filings and registry receipts.

title: Subdividing inherited land among heirs
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Control Act
content: Heirs subdivide only after confirmation of grant with survey, board consent for agricultural land, and new titles per share. Agree boundaries in writing. Keep the confirmed grant and mutation records.

title: Registering long leases
content: Long leases should be registered to bind buyers and lenders with rent, term, and repair terms clear. Keep the registered lease and rent receipts.

title: Leasing out farmland to investors
content: Leasing shambas for farming or masts needs written terms on rent, duration, use, and restoration with registration for long terms. Keep the signed lease and payment records.

title: Creating and registering a land lease — general guidance
content: A lease over registered land in Kenya must generally be in writing and registered to protect a long-term tenant against later buyers or charges. Short leases and key terms such as rent, duration, repair and termination should be clear to both parties before registration. Keep a copy of the signed lease and registration slip.

title: Leasehold tenure and renewals
content: Leaseholds run for fixed terms, commonly 33, 50, or 99 years, with renewal applications before expiry. Check the unexpired term and ground rent. Keep the lease title and renewal records.

title: Legal aid for land grabbing
content: Victims of grabbing or fraudulent transfer facing loss of homes can seek NLAS help with titles, searches, and OB records. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep all ownership documents.

title: Land held for minors
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Registration Act
content: Minors hold land through trustees with court supervision; guardians cannot sell casually. Insist on court approval for dealings. Keep trust and court records.

title: Auction of charged land on default
content: Lenders must issue statutory notices and valuations before auctioning charged land. Borrowers can redeem before the fall of the hammer. Keep demand notices, statements, and sale adverts.

title: Subdivision and mutation forms
content: Subdivisions need survey, mutation approval, and registration of new titles with consent fees. Agree in writing who pays costs. Keep approved mutations and new titles.

title: Neighbour trees and developments
content: Overhanging trees, borehole drilling, and storey developments affecting neighbours need approvals and notice. Complain to NEMA and county planning with photos. Keep approvals and reports.

title: Off-plan plots and projects
content: Off-plan buyers should verify approvals, survey plans, and developer track record with phased payments tied to milestones. Visit the site. Keep approvals, plans, and payment schedules.

title: Public land allocations
content: Public land is allocated through the NLC with part-development and use conditions. Unauthorised occupation risks recovery. Keep allotment letters and compliance records.

title: Quarries and soil extraction near homes
content: Quarrying needs mineral and NEMA approvals with blasting safeguards. Affected residents report cracks and dust with dated photos. Keep structural reports and complaint references.

title: County rates clearance before transfer
content: Transfers need county rates clearance certificates showing arrears paid. Sellers usually clear before completion. Keep clearance certificates and receipts.

title: Land rates, ground rent and clearance certificates — general guidance
content: County land rates and national ground rent must generally be up to date before a transfer is registered, evidenced by a rates clearance or rent certificate. Buyers commonly ask sellers to clear arrears and penalties before completion. Keep clearance certificates, receipts, and search results.

title: Land rates and land rent — general guidance
content: Landowners must pay county land rates and national land rent where applicable, and arrears can block transfers. Confirm clearance certificates at the county and lands office before transacting. Keep clearance receipts.

title: Right to redeem charged land
content: Borrowers may clear arrears and costs to stop a sale at any time before completion. Get the redemption figure in writing. Keep payment proof and lender correspondence.

title: Land Registration Act, 2012
content: The Land Registration Act governs registration of interests in land, including transfers, leases and charges, and the effect of registration on proprietors. Always conduct an official search and verify the seller's ID, title deed, and encumbrances before paying.

title: When land disputes go to tribunals
content: Some controlled tenancies and land rent matters start at tribunals before the ELC. Check the forum on the notice received. Keep notices and tribunal filings.

title: Ground rent disputes
content: Unpaid ground rent blocks transfers and attracts penalties. Confirm statements at the lands office and clear arrears before completion. Keep rent receipts and clearance.

title: Riparian reserves and road reserves
citation: Land Act; Water Act, 2016; survey guidance
content: Building on riparian or road reserves risks demolition without compensation. Verify reserves on survey plans before buying or building. Keep survey reports and approvals.

title: Water frontage and borehole permits
content: Abstraction from rivers or boreholes needs Water Resources Authority permits alongside county connections. Illegal connections attract penalties. Keep permits and bills.

title: Land sale agreements and deposits — general guidance
citation: Law of Contract Act; Land Act, 2012
content: Land sale agreements should be in writing with parties, price, payment schedule, completion date, and default terms. Avoid large cash deposits without a lawyer or escrow, and insist on receipts. Keep the agreement, payment proof, and all messages.

title: How to do an official land search
content: Apply with the title number and owner ID through the registry or Ardhisasa, pay the fee, and collect the search showing owner, size, and encumbrances. Keep the search printout with the agreement.

title: Title search and Ardhisasa — general guidance
content: Before buying land, conduct an official title search, confirm rates and land rent are paid, and inspect the land with the seller's documents. Nairobi and other registries increasingly use the Ardhisasa online platform. Keep search certificates and payment receipts.

title: Sectional and strata titles for flats — general guidance
content: Apartments and mixed developments in Kenya can be held on sectional titles with individual unit titles plus shared ownership of common areas. Owners typically belong to an owners corporation that manages common property, insurance, and service charges. Keep your sectional title, management records, and payment receipts.

title: Service charge disputes in estates
content: Demand budgets and audited accounts where service charges seem excessive, then raise disputes through management and the ELC where needed. Keep demand notes and receipts.

title: Spousal consent on land dealings
content: Dispositions of matrimonial land need written spousal consent. Transactions without it are voidable. Keep consent forms with completion documents.

title: Long occupation and settlement schemes
content: Long occupiers should engage settlement and adjudication programmes rather than force. Keep occupation history, chief letters, and programme records.

title: Valuation for stamp duty
content: Government valuers assess duty on transfers; under-declared prices are adjusted upwards. Budget for duty, registration, and advocate fees. Keep valuation reports and duty receipts.

title: Stamp duty and government valuation on transfers — general guidance
content: Most land transfers and leases attract stamp duty assessed on the value or consideration, often after a government valuation. Parties should budget for duty, valuation, registration, and advocate fees before signing agreements. Keep valuation reports, duty payment receipts, and registration records.

title: Transfer by transmission after death
citation: Law of Succession Act; Land Registration Act
content: Heirs transfer land by transmission with the confirmed grant, IDs, and registry forms rather than sale forms. Pay rates clearance first. Keep the new title and grant.

title: Unlawful occupation — general guidance
content: Unlawful occupation or encroachment on land may be challenged through legal action seeking eviction or compensation. Do not use force or demolish structures without a court order. Keep title proof, photos, demand letters, and witness details.

title: Disputing land valuations
content: Valuation disputes are tested with independent registered valuer reports and comparable sales. Commission a second report where figures diverge. Keep both reports and instructions.

title: Wayleaves for power and water lines
content: Utilities may seek registered wayleaves with compensation for lines crossing land. Negotiate terms before construction. Keep wayleave agreements and payment records.
